The Nigerian Electricity Supply Industry Week has been rescheduled to 13-19 December, 2026, from its earlier 15 November date to align the conference with ongoing power sector reforms. The convener of NESI Week, Dr Obiora Anthony, disclosed this in a statement issued in Abuja, saying the new dates would allow the Federal Ministry of Power, investors and other major stakeholders to harmonise the conference objectives with the power sector reforms of President Bola Tinubu’s administration. The conference is expected to bring together global players in the electricity industry under a public-private partnership framework to strengthen Nigeria’s power infrastructure and improve electricity supply. With the theme, ‘Powering the Future’, the event will provide a platform for policy dialogue, business engagements, investment, innovation and strategic partnerships across the electricity and energy ecosystem. The programme will feature the NESI CEO and Policy Forum, NESI Expo, NESI Innovation Challenge, NESI Energy Future Experience, NESI Games and Awards. It is expected to attract policymakers, industry leaders, investors, innovators and technology providers. Nigerians turn to solar as grid power falters VIDEO: Tinubu arrives Saudi Arabia for Umrah Shettima pledges legal backing, steady salaries for community health workers Anthony said the rescheduling would allow for further coordination with stakeholders and adequate preparation for the programme. He also expressed appreciation for the continued support of partners and prospective participants. He urged sponsors, exhibitors, speakers, media partners and participating institutions to take note of the revised dates. “NESI Week is put together by industry players to deliver electricity and drive growth and development in the sector, translating policy into action for an increase in generation, transmission, and distribution in the power sector value chain,” he said.
